newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to nominate Weld as ambassador to Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to nominate Weld as ambassador to Mexico.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will nominate Massachusetts Gov. William Weld, a Republican, as ambassador to Mexico and will fight congressional opposition to his nomination, the White House said on Wednesday.
"The president is going to stand up and fight for Gov. Weld," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters. "He intends to proceed with the nomination of Gov. Weld as U.S. ambassador to Mexico."

The decision by Clinton, a Democrat, to nominate Weld to be ambassador to Mexico has run into tough opposition from Sen. Jesse Helms, the North Carolina Republican who heads the Senate Foreign Relations Comittee, which approves ambassadors.
Helms, a conservative Republican, has said he objects to Weld's views on marijuana as medicine and said the governor, who is in the moderate wing of the Republican party, is not "ambassador quality."
Weld, however, has said Helms' opposition is political, telling reporters on Tuesday: "In plain language, I am not Sen. Helms's kind of Republican."

The White House had seemed to be backing away from Weld on Tuesday, with McCurry making public statements that suggested the administration might bow to Helms' opposition. Weld fired back later in the day, challenging Clinton to fight for him.

McCurry said White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles had spoken to Weld on Tuesday evening and told him the president would formally proceed with the nomination and would fight for its approval despite the opposition.
"The president reviewed the issue with Erskine last night and said that he wanted the White House to make every effort to secure his nomination," McCurry added.
Asked when Clinton would formally nominate Weld, McCurry replied: "As soon as his paperwork is done."
